sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Project descriptor and dependencies
sections.what: Names the frontend package, lists the commands to develop, build, start and lint it, and lists the libraries it needs at runtime and while developing.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard way for npm to know how to install and run the project.
sections.watch_out: Pinning Next.js exactly while other libraries use loose ranges means upgrades will behave unevenly.

summary: The project's descriptor listing the frontend's name, its run and build commands, and the libraries it depends on.
purpose: Tells npm which libraries to install and which commands start, build and lint the frontend.
why: Likely reason: standard for a Node.js project. Reason for listing these specific libraries is not stated in the code.
how: npm reads the name and version, then the scripts, the runtime dependencies, and the development-only tools. Running install downloads them.
inputs: Commands typed by a developer, such as install, dev, build or start.
outputs: A set of installed libraries and runnable commands.
risks: Several listed libraries such as axios, react-query and tailwindcss do not appear in the visible frontend code, so they add weight without visible use. Version ranges can pull in newer releases that behave differently.
debug: If install fails, check the version numbers and whether the Node.js version matches the Docker image. If a command is missing, check the scripts section.
